items.cn: flight 也指逃离危险。

items.en: Flight named a scheduled air journey and a run of stairs.
items.cn: flight 指定期航班和一段楼梯。

note.en: Flight is compared with similar-looking words and with words for journeys and escape.
note.cn: 把 flight 与形近词以及表示行程和逃跑的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Flight is a stretch of moving through air: a plane trip, the flying itself, an escape, or a run of stairs.
normalIntro.cn: flight 是一段穿行空中的路程：航班、飞行、逃跑，或一段楼梯。

normal.en: Our flight leaves at noon.
The bird was in flight.
They took flight when the alarm rang.
The office is two flights up.
normal.cn: 办公室在上两段楼梯处。

normal.en: A flight attendant greeted us.

abstract.en: Flight is distance made by leaving the ground.
abstract.cn: 飞行是离开地面所走的距离。

abstract.en: Escape and flying share the same image.
abstract.cn: 逃跑与飞翔共享同一个意象。

abstract.en: Every stair is a small flight upward.
abstract.cn: 每一段楼梯都是一次向上的小小飞行。

examples.en: Our flight was delayed by heavy snow.
examples.cn: 我们的航班因大雪延误了。

examples.en: The flight lasted six hours.
examples.cn: 飞行持续了六个小时。

examples.en: She climbed three flights of stairs.
examples.cn: 她爬了三段楼梯。

dict_mnemonic.text: flight 是古英语 fleogan（飞）的名词，核心义「飞行的过程」，由此得到航班、逃跑与一段楼梯。

root: 源自古英语 flyht（飞行），与 fleogan（飞）同源，核心义「在空中划过的一段路」。

sensesIntro.en: Flight means an air journey, the act of flying, an escape, or a set of stairs.
sensesIntro.cn: flight 意为航班、飞行、逃跑或一段楼梯。

core.en: A continuous passage through air or upward.
core.cn: 在空中或向上的一段连续行程。

branches.en: A scheduled trip by plane.
branches.cn: 按计划乘飞机的一次行程。

branches.en: The act of moving through air.
Running away as if taking wing.
A continuous run of steps.
Flying and fleeing share one image.
branches.cn: 飞行与逃跑共享一个意象。

intro.en: Flight builds words for air travel, paths, and things that cannot fly.
intro.cn: flight 构成表示空中旅行、航线和不能飞行的词。

latinIntro.en: Flight has no Latin ancestor; Latin volatus, a flying, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: flight 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 volatus（飞行）只是语义对应词。

items.exampleCN: 太空飞行始于六十年代。

items.meaning: to test an aircraft in the air
items.exampleCN: 他们对新飞机进行试飞。

definition_zh: 羊群；鸟群；人群；聚集
definition_en: a group of sheep or birds, a crowd of people, or to gather in large numbers
core_image: 一群羊挤成一团，沿山坡缓缓移动
scene: 一群羊在山坡上吃草。A flock of sheep grazed on the hill.
sceneCN: 这里 flock 是「羊群」（第 1 个义项）；句意：一群羊在山坡上吃草。

senses.title: Group of sheep
senses.definition: a group of sheep or similar animals kept together
senses.definitionCN: 养在一起的一群羊或类似动物
senses.example: A flock of sheep grazed on the hill.
senses.exampleCN: 一群羊在山坡上吃草。
senses.why: This is the oldest and most concrete sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老也最具体的义项。

senses.title: Group of birds
senses.definition: a group of birds flying or feeding together
senses.definitionCN: 一起飞行或觅食的一群鸟
senses.example: A flock of geese crossed the sky.
senses.exampleCN: 一群大雁飞过天空。
senses.why: The word extends to other animals that stay together.
senses.whyCN: 这个词扩展到其他群居动物。

senses.title: Crowd
senses.definition: a large group of people, often moving together
senses.definitionCN: 一大群常常一起行动的人
senses.example: A flock of fans waited outside.
senses.exampleCN: 一大群粉丝在外面等候。
senses.why: People behaving like sheep are called a flock.
senses.whyCN: 像羊一样行动的人群被称作 flock。

senses.title: Gather
senses.definition: to move or gather in large numbers
senses.definitionCN: 大批地移动或聚集
senses.example: Tourists flock to the beach in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 夏天游客涌向海滩。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb of crowding together.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为成群聚集的动词。

intro.en: Flock is an Old English word, flocc, meaning a group or troop.
intro.cn: flock 是古英语词 flocc，意为群体或队伍。

items.en: Flocc meant a group of people or animals.
items.cn: flocc 指一群人或动物。

items.en: The word was used for sheep and birds.
items.cn: 这个词用于羊群和鸟群。

items.en: Flock also named a Christian congregation.
items.cn: flock 也指基督教会的会众。

items.en: The verb meant to gather in numbers.
items.cn: 动词形式意为成群聚集。

items.en: Flock is used for crowds of people.
items.cn: flock 用于形容人群。

note.en: Flock is compared with similar-looking words and with words for groups of animals.
note.cn: 把 flock 与形近词以及表示动物群体的词作比较。

entries.definition: to move with a quick motion

normalIntro.en: A flock is a group that moves as one: sheep, birds, or people drawn to the same place.
normalIntro.cn: flock 是作为一个整体移动的群体：羊、鸟，或被同一地方吸引的人。

normal.en: The flock moved down the hill.
Birds gathered in a large flock.
Fans flocked to the concert.
The shepherd counts his flock.
Sheep flock together for safety.
normal.cn: 羊群聚在一起以求安全。

abstract.en: A crowd can think like a flock.
abstract.cn: 人群的思维可以像羊群。

abstract.en: Following is easy inside a group.
abstract.cn: 在群体中跟随是容易的。

abstract.en: The shepherd knows the group by counting.
abstract.cn: 牧人通过计数来了解群体。

examples.en: A flock of sheep grazed on the hill.
examples.cn: 一群羊在山坡上吃草。

examples.en: A flock of geese crossed the sky.
examples.cn: 一群大雁飞过天空。

examples.en: Tourists flock to the beach in summer.
examples.cn: 夏天游客涌向海滩。

dict_mnemonic.text: flock 源自古英语 flocc（群体），核心义「聚成一群」，由羊群推及鸟群、人群与成群行动。

root: 源自古英语 flocc（群体、队伍），核心义「聚在一起的一群」。

sensesIntro.en: Flock means a group of sheep, birds, or people, or to gather in numbers.
sensesIntro.cn: flock 意为羊群、鸟群、人群，或成群聚集。

core.en: A group moving and staying together.
core.cn: 一起移动并待在一起的群体。

branches.en: Sheep kept and moved together.
Birds flying as one body.
branches.cn: 作为一个整体飞行的鸟。

branches.en: People gathered like animals.
The act of crowding toward a place.
Animal groups and human crowds share the word.
branches.cn: 动物群与人群共用一个词。

intro.en: Flock builds a small family around groups and gathering.
intro.cn: flock 围绕群体与聚集构成一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: Flock has no Latin ancestor; Latin grex, a herd, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: flock 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 grex（群）只是语义对应词。

items.example: The lamb stayed near its flockmate.

items.meaning: a record of a sheep flock
items.exampleCN: 农场主保存羊群谱系册。

definition_zh: 植物群；植物志；（人体）菌群
definition_en: the plant species of a region taken together; a book that lists them; the microbes living in or on a body
core_image: 一本按名字排列的名册，每个名字背后都站着一种真实生长的植物
scene: 岛上有些蕨类只在此处生长，别处找不到；植物志把它们逐一记下，供后来者比对。The island's flora includes ferns found nowhere else.
sceneCN: 这里 flora 指「一个地区植物物种的总和」（第 1 个义项：把一地植物种类整体看待）；句意为这座岛的植物群中有别处找不到的蕨类。

senses.title: All plant species of a region
senses.titleCN: 一个地区植物种类的总和
senses.definition: the whole set of plant species growing in a region
senses.definitionCN: 某一地区生长的全部植物物种
senses.example: The island's flora includes ferns found nowhere else.
senses.exampleCN: 这座岛的植物群中有别处找不到的蕨类。
senses.why: Flora began as the name of a goddess; naturalists then used it for the whole roll-call of plants in one place.
senses.whyCN: flora 原是女神之名；博物学家随后用它指一个地方全部植物的名录。

senses.title: A book listing those plants
senses.definition: a book or catalogue describing the plants of an area
senses.definitionCN: 描述某地植物的书或名录
senses.example: The county flora runs to eight hundred pages.
senses.exampleCN: 该郡的植物志长达八百页。
senses.why: The title of a catalogue was read as the name of its subject, so the same word names both the plants and the volume about them.
senses.whyCN: 书名被读成所写对象的名字，于是同一个词既指植物，也指写它们的书。

senses.title: Microbes of the gut
senses.definition: the community of bacteria living in the intestines
senses.definitionCN: 生活在肠道里的细菌群落
senses.example: Antibiotics can disturb the gut flora for months.
senses.exampleCN: 抗生素可能扰动肠道菌群数月。
senses.why: Medicine extended the plant-roll-call image to invisible residents: a body, too, has a local list of species.
senses.whyCN: 医学把这套「地方物种名录」的意象扩展到看不见的居民：身体也有一份本地物种清单。

senses.title: Microbes of skin or mouth
senses.titleCN: 皮肤或口腔的微生物群
senses.definition: the resident microbes of a body surface or cavity
senses.definitionCN: 体表或腔内的常驻微生物
senses.example: The skin flora shifts with soap and humidity.
senses.exampleCN: 皮肤菌群随肥皂与湿度而变。
senses.why: Each body surface keeps its own roster, so clinicians speak of a flora rather than a single germ.
senses.whyCN: 每个体表都保有自己的名册，因此临床说的是「菌群」而非单一细菌。

senses.title: The study of regional plant lists
senses.titleCN: 研究地区植物名录的学问
senses.definition: the branch of botany that compares the species lists of regions
senses.definitionCN: 比较各地区物种名录的植物学分支
senses.example: Floristics maps where each species first appears.
senses.exampleCN: 植物区系学标出每个物种首次出现的地方。
senses.why: Once lists exist, they can be compared, and comparison becomes a discipline with its own name.
senses.whyCN: 名录一旦存在就可以比较，而比较本身成为一门有名字的学问。

senses.title: Plants of a past period
senses.titleCN: 某一地质时期的植物群
senses.definition: the plant species reconstructed for a past geological period
senses.definitionCN: 重建出的某一地质时期的植物物种
senses.example: The fossil flora is dominated by seed ferns.
senses.exampleCN: 这一化石植物群以种子蕨为主。
senses.why: Fossils are read as a former roll-call, so a vanished world gets a flora of its own.
senses.whyCN: 化石被读作一份过去的点名册，消失的世界于是也有了自己的植物群。

senses.title: The Roman goddess of flowers
senses.definition: the Roman goddess of flowers and spring
senses.definitionCN: 罗马神话中司花与春天的女神
senses.example: The festival honoured Flora with garlands.
senses.exampleCN: 节庆用花环致敬花神。
senses.why: The common noun comes straight from the goddess, whose name already meant flower.
senses.whyCN: 这个普通名词直接来自女神之名，而女神之名本义就是花。

senses.title: Plants and animals named together
senses.titleCN: 与动物并称时的植物一侧
senses.definition: plants as one half of the pair flora and fauna
senses.definitionCN: 作为「动植物」一对中的植物一侧
senses.example: The reserve protects its flora and fauna alike.
senses.exampleCN: 保护区对动植物一并加以保护。
senses.why: Pairing the two Roman names gives a compact formula for all living things in a place.
senses.whyCN: 把两个罗马名字配对，就得到一个指一地全部生物的紧凑说法。

intro.en: Flora is the Roman goddess of flowers; her name comes from Latin flos, florem 'flower'. The botanical sense is early modern.
intro.cn: flora 是罗马的花神；其名来自拉丁 flos、florem「花」。植物学义属近代早期。

items.en: Flos, florem meant 'flower, blossom'. Its deeper origin is not established, and the forms sometimes proposed for it are reconstructions.
items.cn: flos、florem 意为「花、开花」。其更深来源没有定论，有时为它提出的形式都是重构形式。

items.en: Flora was the goddess of flowers and of spring; her festival was the Floralia.
items.cn: Flora 是司花与春天的女神，她的节庆是花神节。

items.en: Early modern botanists titled their catalogues after her, and the book title slid into the sense 'plants of a region'.
items.cn: 近代早期植物学家用她的名字给名录命名，书名又滑入「一地的植物」之义。

items.en: From the late nineteenth century medicine applied the word to the resident microbes of gut, skin and mouth.
items.cn: 19 世纪后期起，医学把这个词用于肠道、皮肤与口腔的常驻微生物。

items.en: Flora and fauna became a fixed pair in English for the living things of a place.
items.cn: flora and fauna 在英语中成为指一地生物的固定搭配。

items.en: Source uncertain (root and first date): the pre-Latin origin of flos is unsettled, and the first English use of flora for regional plants is dated only approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根与首见年代）：flos 在拉丁语之前的来源未定；flora 指地区植物在英语中的首用年代只有约数。

note.en: Group one separates look-alikes that share the flower root from one that does not; group two holds the ecological neighbours.
note.cn: 第一组区分共用「花」词根的外形相近词与一个不同源词；第二组是生态学上的邻近词。

entries.definition: From flos: relating to flowers, as a floral scent; it describes flowers, not a species list.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 flos：与花有关的，如花香；它描述花，不指物种名录。

entries.definition: From floridus 'flowing with flowers': once 'flowering', now 'ornate' or 'ruddy'.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 floridus「开满花的」：曾指「开花的」，今指「华丽」或「脸色红润」。

entries.definition: Originally the flower, the finest part of ground grain; the spelling split off with the food sense.
entries.definitionCN: 原指「花」，即磨碎谷物最精细的部分；拼写随食物义分化。

entries.definition: From Old English flor 'ground, pavement', unrelated to flos; only the sound matches.
entries.definitionCN: 来自古英语 flor「地面、铺地」，与 flos 无关，只有读音相同。

entries.definition: The living plant cover of a place; flora is the species roll-call behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 指一地活生生的植物覆盖；flora 是它背后的物种名录。

entries.definition: The animal species of a region, paired with flora but never a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 指一地的动物物种，与 flora 配对，却从不同义。

entries.definition: An everyday neutral phrase; flora is its technical and bookish counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 日常中性说法；flora 是它的技术、书面对应词。

entries.definition: The variety of living things measured as a count; flora is one roster within that total.
entries.definitionCN: 按数量衡量的生物多样性；flora 是这一总数中的一份名录。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations are the real Latin root, the real goddess and the real collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用真实拉丁词根、真实神名与真实搭配。

normal.en: Latin flos 'flower' gives Flora, floral, florist, floriculture and flora itself.
normal.cn: 拉丁 flos「花」给出 Flora、floral、florist、floriculture 与 flora。

normal.en: The family: floral, florist, floriculture, floristics.
Fixed phrases: native flora, local flora, gut flora, flora and fauna.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：本土植物群、地方植物群、肠道菌群、动植物。

normal.en: The goddess Flora lent her name to catalogues, and the catalogue lent it to the plants.
normal.cn: 花神 Flora 把名字借给名录，名录又把名字借给植物。

normal.en: Medicine reuses it for microbes, giving gut flora and skin flora.
normal.cn: 医学把它再用到微生物，于是有肠道菌群与皮肤菌群。

abstract.en: Picture a region's plants standing in a queue, each waiting to be named.
abstract.cn: 想象一个地区的植物排成队，等着被点名。

abstract.en: Picture the word as a passport listing every species allowed to live in one country.
abstract.cn: 想象这个词是一本护照，列出允许居留于一国的每个物种。

abstract.en: Picture a body as a garden with its own invisible planting list.
abstract.cn: 想象身体是一座花园，有自己的隐形种植清单。

examples.en: The flora of the wetlands includes three protected orchids.
examples.cn: 湿地植物群中有三种受保护的兰花。

examples.en: She wrote the flora of the whole archipelago.
examples.cn: 她写下了整个群岛的植物志。

examples.en: A high-fibre diet feeds a healthier gut flora.
examples.cn: 高纤维饮食养出更健康的肠道菌群。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「弗洛拉（Flora）花神」——花神手里的花名册 → 植物群；植物志

root: 拉丁 flos、florem「花」，罗马花神 Flora 即由此得名；flos 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with the goddess and her flower name, pass through the species list and the book that holds it, then extend to microbes and to a paired formula for all life.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从花神与「花」这个词开始，经过物种名录与承载名录的书，再扩展到微生物，最后成为指全部生物的配对说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a roll-call of flowers, written down and then applied to any living roster.
core.cn: 核心意象：一份花的点名册，先被写下来，再被用于任何活物的名册。

branches.en: LIST AND BOOK: the plants and the volume about them share one name.
branches.cn: 名录与书：植物本身与写它们的书共用一个名字。

branches.en: INVISIBLE RESIDENTS: the roster moves from forests to the body's microbes.
branches.cn: 看不见的居民：名册从森林移到体内的微生物。

branches.en: COMPARE ACROSS TIME: species lists of regions and of past periods can both be compared.
branches.cn: 跨时间比较：地区名录与过去时期的名录都能拿来比较。

branches.en: GODDESS: the proper name is the source of the common noun.
branches.cn: 神名：专名是普通名词的来源。

branches.en: PAIR: flora beside fauna names all life in a place.
branches.cn: 配对：flora 与 fauna 并称，指一地全部生物。

intro.en: Flora and its family descend from one Latin noun for flower, with suffixes marking adjective, person and craft.
intro.cn: flora 及其词族都出自一个指「花」的拉丁名词，后缀标出形容词、人物与技艺。

latinIntro.en: Latin flos, florem 'flower' yields Flora, floralis, floricultura; -alis, -ista and -cultura build the derivatives.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 flos、florem「花」给出 Flora、floralis、floricultura；-alis、-ista 与 -cultura 构成派生词。

items.example: The root names the part that makes seed.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指结种的那一部分。
它把 floralis 变成 floral。

items.example: A floral scent filled the room.
It gives florist, a flower seller.

items.exampleCN: 花艺师给花茎缠了铁丝。
花卉栽培是一门大生意。
植物区系学比较物种名录。

definition_zh: 繁荣；挥动；花饰；夸张动作
definition_en: to grow or succeed well, to wave something in the air, or a showy decorative movement
core_image: 乐手把琴弓向上一挑，收在一个漂亮的动作里
scene: 小生意在城里兴旺起来。The small business flourished in the city.
sceneCN: 这里 flourish 是「兴旺」（第 1 个义项）；句意：小生意在城里兴旺起来。

senses.title: Grow well
senses.definition: to grow strongly and healthily
senses.definitionCN: 茁壮而健康地生长
senses.example: The plants flourish in warm rain.
senses.exampleCN: 植物在暖雨中长得茂盛。
senses.why: This is the original sense of flowering.
senses.whyCN: 这是开花的本义。

senses.title: Succeed
senses.definition: to be successful or active
senses.definitionCN: 成功或活跃地发展
senses.example: The small business flourished in the city.
senses.exampleCN: 小生意在城里兴旺起来。
senses.why: A growing plant became a metaphor for success.
senses.whyCN: 生长的植物被隐喻为成功。

senses.title: Wave
senses.definition: to hold something up and move it about
senses.definitionCN: 举起某物并来回挥动
senses.example: He flourished the letter in triumph.
senses.exampleCN: 他得意地挥动那封信。
senses.why: A showy gesture is like a plant waving in the air.
senses.whyCN: 夸张的手势像植物在空中摆动。

senses.title: Decorative movement
senses.definition: a showy curve or gesture added for effect
senses.definitionCN: 为效果添加的夸张曲线或动作
senses.example: She signed with a flourish.
senses.exampleCN: 她签名时带了一个花饰。
senses.why: The noun names the flourish of a pen or hand.
senses.whyCN: 名词指笔或手的华彩动作。

intro.en: Flourish comes from Latin florere, to bloom, from flos, a flower.
intro.cn: flourish 源自拉丁语 florere（开花），来自 flos（花）。

items.en: Flos meant a flower.
items.cn: flos 意为花。

items.en: Florere meant to bloom or prosper.
items.cn: florere 意为开花或繁荣。

items.en: Florir meant to bloom or thrive.
items.cn: florir 意为开花或兴旺。

items.en: Flourish meant to bloom and succeed.
items.cn: flourish 意为开花与兴盛。

items.en: The word named a showy gesture or decoration.
items.cn: 这个词开始指夸张的动作或装饰。

note.en: Flourish is compared with similar-looking words and with words for thriving.
note.cn: 把 flourish 与形近词以及表示兴旺的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Flourish is to bloom: plants, businesses, and hands all can do it.
normalIntro.cn: flourish 就是开花：植物、生意和手都能做出这个动作。

normal.en: The garden flourishes in spring.
Trade flourished after the war.
He flourished his hat.
She bowed with a flourish.
A flourish of trumpets opened the show.

abstract.en: What flourishes needs room, light, and patience.
abstract.cn: 繁茂需要空间、光和耐心。

abstract.en: A gesture can say what a word cannot.
abstract.cn: 一个动作能说出语言说不出的话。

abstract.en: The same word describes a plant and a pen.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既描述植物也描述笔。

examples.en: The small business flourished in the city.
examples.cn: 小生意在城里兴旺起来。

examples.en: The plants flourish in warm rain.
examples.cn: 植物在暖雨中长得茂盛。

examples.en: She signed with a flourish.
examples.cn: 她签名时带了一个花饰。

dict_mnemonic.text: flourish 源自拉丁语 florere（开花），核心义「像花一样展开」，由植物繁茂引申为事业兴旺与挥洒的动作。

root: 源自拉丁语 flos（花）与 florere（开花），核心义「像花一样盛开」。

sensesIntro.en: Flourish means to grow well, to succeed, to wave something, or a showy gesture.
sensesIntro.cn: flourish 意为繁茂、兴旺、挥动某物或夸张的花饰动作。

core.en: To open out like a flower.
core.cn: 像花一样展开。

branches.en: Plants growing strongly.
A business opening out.
A hand waving something grandly.
An added curve of style.
Plants and fortunes bloom alike.
branches.cn: 植物与运势以同样方式盛开。

intro.en: Flourish belongs to the Latin flor- family of flowers and blooming.
intro.cn: flourish 属于拉丁语 flor- 这一表示花与开花的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin flos and florere are the direct ancestors of the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 flos 与 florere 是该词族的直接来源。

items.exampleCN: 这座镇子每年夏天都兴旺。

items.example: The flourisher waved a bright flag.
He writes in a florid style.

latinEntries.example: Flos is the root of the flor- family.
latinEntries.exampleCN: flos 是 flor- 词族的词根。

definition_zh: 流动；流量；车流；源自
definition_en: to move steadily like water, or a steady movement or supply of something
core_image: 河水绕过石头，连成一条不停的线
scene: 河水缓缓流过石桥。The river flows slowly under the stone bridge.
sceneCN: 这里 flow 是「流动」（第 1 个义项）；句意：河水缓缓流过石桥。

senses.title: Move like water
senses.definition: to move steadily in a stream
senses.definitionCN: 像水流一样稳定移动
senses.example: The river flows slowly under the stone bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 河水缓缓流过石桥。
senses.why: This is the core physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心的物理义项。

senses.title: Steady movement
senses.definition: a continuous movement of people, goods, or information
senses.definitionCN: 人、货物或信息的持续移动
senses.example: The flow of traffic was heavy.
senses.exampleCN: 车流很密集。
senses.why: Water became a model for any continuous movement.
senses.whyCN: 水成为任何持续运动的模型。

senses.title: Arise from
senses.definition: to come from a source
senses.definitionCN: 从某个来源产生
senses.example: Many problems flow from poor planning.
senses.exampleCN: 许多问题源于计划不周。
senses.why: A river flows from its source, and so does a result.
senses.whyCN: 河流从源头流出，结果也从原因流出。

senses.title: Supply
senses.definition: the rate at which something is supplied
senses.definitionCN: 某物被供给的速率
senses.example: They measured the flow of water.
senses.exampleCN: 他们测量了水流量。
senses.why: The movement measured over time is a flow.
senses.whyCN: 随时间计量的运动就是流量。

intro.en: Flow comes from Old English flowan, a Germanic verb for moving like water.
intro.cn: flow 源自古英语 flowan，是日耳曼语中表示像水一样移动的动词。

items.en: The root meant to flow or stream.
items.cn: 这个词根意为流动或涌流。

items.en: Flowan meant to move like water.
items.cn: flowan 意为像水一样移动。

items.en: Flow also named a rising tide.
items.cn: flow 也指上涨的潮水。

items.en: The noun named a steady movement.
items.cn: 名词形式指稳定的运动。

items.en: The word extended to traffic, money, and ideas.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到交通、金钱和思想。

note.en: Flow is compared with similar-looking words and with words for moving liquid.
note.cn: 把 flow 与形近词以及表示液体运动的词作比较。

entries.definition: to flow, as a tap does

normalIntro.en: Flow is one continuous line of movement, of water, traffic, money, or causes.
normalIntro.cn: flow 是一条连续的运动线：水、交通、金钱或原因。

normal.en: The river flows to the sea.
Traffic flows better after the fix.
Cash flow keeps a business alive.
Good results flow from good habits.
The tide ebbs and flows.

abstract.en: Water teaches that movement needs a channel.
abstract.cn: 水告诉我们运动需要通道。

abstract.en: Blocked flow builds pressure.
abstract.cn: 被阻断的流动会积聚压力。

abstract.en: Every result has a source upstream.
abstract.cn: 每个结果在上游都有源头。

examples.en: The river flows slowly under the stone bridge.
examples.cn: 河水缓缓流过石桥。

examples.en: The flow of traffic was heavy.
examples.cn: 车流很密集。

examples.en: Many problems flow from poor planning.
examples.cn: 许多问题源于计划不周。

dict_mnemonic.text: flow 源自古英语 flowan（流动），与 flood、fleet 同根，核心义「像水一样连续移动」。

root: 源自古英语 flowan（流动），核心义「连续不断的移动」。

sensesIntro.en: Flow means to move like water, a steady movement, a rate of supply, or to arise from.
sensesIntro.cn: flow 意为像水一样流动、持续运动、供给流量或源自某处。

core.en: Continuous movement along a course.
core.cn: 沿通道的连续运动。

branches.en: Water moving in a stream.
Traffic or goods in motion.
A result coming from a cause.
The measured rate of supply.
Rivers and reasons both have sources.

intro.en: Flow builds words for directions, instruments, and excess.
intro.cn: flow 构成表示方向、仪器和过量的词。

latinIntro.en: Flow has no Latin ancestor; Latin fluere, to flow, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: flow 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 fluere（流）只是语义对应词。

items.example: The river flowed over the bank.
The flowing water cut the stone.
The outflow of money worried them.

definition_zh: 波动；起伏；变动；来回变化
definition_en: to rise and fall or change irregularly in level, amount, or quality
core_image: 水面一起一伏的波浪线
scene: 菜市场的价格牌早晚各换一次，蔬菜筐旁的箭头一上一下。 Because of supply and demand, vegetable prices fluctuated a lot this week, and the labels changed morning and evening.
sceneCN: 这里 fluctuate 是「上下波动、起伏不定」（第 1 个义项：价格不规则地涨落）；句意：受供需影响，这周蔬菜价格波动很大，标价早晚都在变。

collocations.zh: 在 A 与 B 之间来回变动

derivatives.zh: 波动的；起伏的（医学中也指可移动的）

senses.title: Prices rise and fall
senses.definition: of prices or values, to go up and down repeatedly and irregularly
senses.definitionCN: 指价格或价值反复而不规则地涨落
senses.example: Oil prices fluctuated all summer.
senses.exampleCN: 整个夏天油价都在波动。
senses.why: Latin fluctuare is 'to move in waves', from fluctus 'a wave'. A price that rises and falls draws the same up-and-down line as a wave.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 fluctuare 意为“像波浪一样运动”，来自 fluctus“波浪”。涨落的价格画出的正是波浪一样的上下曲线。

senses.title: Levels vary over time
senses.definition: of a level such as temperature or water, to keep changing within a range
senses.definitionCN: 指温度、水位等水平在一定范围内持续变化
senses.example: The lake level fluctuates with the seasons.
senses.exampleCN: 湖面水位随季节起伏。
senses.why: Water is the literal source of the image, so a level that rises and falls is the most natural application of the verb.
senses.whyCN: 水是这个意象的字面来源，因此水位的升降是这个动词最自然的用法。

senses.title: Numbers swing
senses.definition: of figures such as rates or sales, to change repeatedly in either direction
senses.definitionCN: 指利率、销量等数字反复朝两个方向变化
senses.example: Sales fluctuate from month to month.
senses.exampleCN: 销量逐月波动。
senses.why: A rate or a sales figure is plotted as a line, and a line that keeps swinging looks like a wave.
senses.whyCN: 利率或销量被画成一条线，反复摆动的线看起来就像波浪。

senses.title: Quality or attendance varies
senses.titleCN: 质量或出勤率时好时坏
senses.definition: of a non-numeric quality, to be uneven from one time or case to another
senses.definitionCN: 指非数字性的质量在不同时间或情形下不均衡
senses.example: The quality of the meals fluctuates.
senses.exampleCN: 饭菜的质量时好时坏。
senses.why: Anything measured on a scale can be plotted as a wave, even when the scale is subjective, like quality or turnout.
senses.whyCN: 任何按尺度衡量的东西都能画成波浪，即使尺度是主观的，如质量或出席人数。

senses.title: Opinions and moods shift
senses.definition: of feelings or opinions, to change back and forth
senses.definitionCN: 指情绪或意见来回改变
senses.example: Public opinion fluctuated during the campaign.
senses.exampleCN: 竞选期间公众意见摇摆不定。
senses.why: The wave image moves from water to the mind: feelings rise and fall without settling at one level.
senses.whyCN: 波浪意象从水面移向心智：情绪起起伏伏，不停在某一水平。

senses.title: Fluctuate between two states
senses.definition: to move repeatedly from one condition to another, as in 'fluctuate between hope and fear'
senses.definitionCN: 反复从一种状态转到另一种，如“在希望与恐惧之间摇摆”
senses.example: He fluctuated between hope and despair.
senses.exampleCN: 他在希望与绝望之间摇摆。
senses.why: A wave has a crest and a trough; to fluctuate between two things is to keep moving from one extreme to the other.
senses.whyCN: 波浪有波峰和波谷；在两者之间 fluctuate，就是在两个极端之间不断移动。

senses.title: Move like a wave
senses.definition: in literary or technical use, to move in a wavelike way
senses.definitionCN: 在文学或技术用法中，像波浪一样运动
senses.example: The surface of the pool fluctuated in the wind.
senses.exampleCN: 池面在风中起伏。
senses.why: This is the original physical sense, now rarer in English but still present in technical writing.
senses.whyCN: 这是原本的物理义项，现代英语中较少见，但仍存在于技术写作中。

senses.title: Economic activity varies
senses.definition: of an economy, currency, or market, to expand and contract irregularly
senses.definitionCN: 指经济、货币或市场不规则地扩张与收缩
senses.example: The currency fluctuated against the dollar.
senses.exampleCN: 该货币对美元的汇率起伏不定。
senses.why: Markets are described as waves in economics, so the verb naturally covers currencies and activity.
senses.whyCN: 经济学把市场描述为波浪，因此这个动词自然覆盖货币与经济活动。

intro.en: Fluctuate is a Latin verb built on fluctus 'a wave', from fluere 'to flow'. The etymology is clear and the 'wave' image is the key to every sense.
intro.cn: fluctuate 是建立在 fluctus“波浪”之上的拉丁动词，来自 fluere“流动”。词源清楚，“波浪”意象是理解所有义项的关键。

items.en: First recorded in English, from Latin fluctuatus, past participle of fluctuare 'to undulate, move in waves'.
items.cn: 最早记录于 17 世纪 30 年代，来自拉丁语 fluctuatus，即 fluctuare“起伏、像波浪般运动”的过去分词。

items.en: Fluctuare is from fluctus 'a wave, billow, surge, a flowing', which comes from the past-participle stem of fluere 'to flow'.
items.cn: fluctuare 来自 fluctus“波浪、巨浪、涌动、流动”，后者来自 fluere“流动”的过去分词词干。

items.en: Fluere comes from an extended form of PIE *bhleu- 'to swell, well up, overflow', itself an extension of *bhel- (2) 'to blow, swell'.
items.cn: fluere 来自原始印欧语 *bhleu-“膨胀、涌起、溢出”的扩展形式，后者又是 *bhel-（第 2 义）“吹、膨胀”的扩展。

items.en: The same root gives fluent, fluid, flux, influence, influx, superfluous and mellifluous; all carry the image of flowing.
items.cn: 同一词根产生 fluent、fluid、flux、influence、influx、superfluous、mellifluous；它们都带着“流动”的意象。

items.en: The verb extends from water to prices, rates, moods, currencies and economies. The noun fluctuation keeps the wave image explicit.
items.cn: 这个动词从水面延伸到价格、比率、情绪、货币和经济。名词 fluctuation 保留了明确的波浪意象。

note.en: Look-alikes share the flowing root; near meanings differ in whether the movement is up and down, back and forth, or simply changing.
note.cn: 形近词共享“流动”词根；近义词的区别在于运动是上下、来回，还是单纯变化。

entries.definition: an instance of rising and falling. It is fluctuate + -ion.
entries.definitionCN: 一次起伏、波动。它是 fluctuate + -ion。

entries.definition: flowing easily, especially of speech. It shares fluere 'to flow' but has nothing to do with rising and falling.
entries.definitionCN: 流畅的，尤指言语。它共享 fluere“流动”，但与上下起伏无关。

entries.definition: a substance that flows; also 'changeable'. The adjective sense overlaps with fluctuating but does not imply repeated rise and fall.
entries.definitionCN: 流体；也指“易变的”。其形容词义与 fluctuating 重叠，但不含反复升降之意。

entries.definition: continuous change; also a flow or discharge. It names the flow itself rather than the up-and-down movement.
entries.definitionCN: 不断变化；也指流动或通量。它指流动本身，而不是上下运动。

entries.definition: to change or differ. It is broader and does not require a repeated up-and-down pattern.
entries.definitionCN: 变化；不同。它更宽泛，不要求反复上下波动。

entries.definition: to swing regularly between two points. It is more mechanical and regular than fluctuate.
entries.definitionCN: 在两点之间规律摆动。它比 fluctuate 更机械、更规则。

entries.definition: to be uncertain or unsteady, especially in opinion. It stresses hesitation, while fluctuate stresses changing level.
entries.definitionCN: 犹豫不决；动摇，尤指意见。它强调迟疑，而 fluctuate 强调水平变化。

entries.definition: to move back and forth in a wide arc. It is more physical and usually larger than a fluctuation.
entries.definitionCN: 大幅度来回摆动。它更物理，幅度通常比 fluctuation 大。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real fluere / fluctus wave image and the real related words.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的 fluere / fluctus 波浪意象和相关词。

normal.en: fluctus means 'wave': anything that rises and falls like water fluctuates.
normal.cn: fluctus 意为“波浪”：任何像水一样起落的东西都在 fluctuate。

normal.en: Fluent, fluid, flux and fluctuate all come from fluere 'to flow'; the wave is the shape the flow makes.
normal.cn: fluent、fluid、flux、fluctuate 都来自 fluere“流动”；波浪是流动形成的形状。

normal.en: Fluctuation is the noun: a price chart with peaks and troughs shows fluctuation.
normal.cn: fluctuation 是名词：有峰有谷的价格图显示的就是波动。

normal.en: Fluctuate between hope and fear is to move from one crest to the other without settling.
normal.cn: 在希望与恐惧之间 fluctuate，就是从一个波峰移到另一个波峰，始终不停定。

normal.en: A fluctuating demand curve is one that will not stay flat.
normal.cn: fluctuating demand 就是无法保持平直的需求曲线。

abstract.en: Picture a cork on water: it rises, falls, rises again, never resting at one height. That cork is fluctuating.
abstract.cn: 想象水面上的软木塞：升起、落下、再升起，从不停在一个高度。这个软木塞就在 fluctuate。

abstract.en: Picture a graph line that looks like a wave: every peak and trough is one fluctuation.
abstract.cn: 想象一条像波浪的图表线：每个峰和谷都是一次 fluctuation。

abstract.en: Picture a mood that lifts and drops with the day: feelings fluctuate like weather.
abstract.cn: 想象随一天起落的情绪：心情像天气一样 fluctuate。

examples.en: Demand for the product fluctuates with the seasons.
examples.cn: 该产品的需求随季节波动。

examples.en: Her weight fluctuated by only two kilos.
examples.cn: 她的体重只在两公斤内波动。

examples.en: The exchange rate has fluctuated sharply since the announcement.
examples.cn: 自公告以来汇率剧烈波动。

dict_mnemonic.text: “弗拉克图埃特”——弗拉克图像波浪一样上上下下 → fluctuate 波动、起伏

root: 拉丁 fluere“流动”→ fluctus“波浪”→ fluctuare“像波浪般起伏”，核心是“上下波动”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of fluctuate all keep the shape of a wave: something rises, falls, and rises again without settling. Prices, water, numbers, moods and markets can all draw that line.
sensesIntro.cn: fluctuate 的八个义项都保留波浪的形状：某物升起、落下、再升起，始终不定。价格、水位、数字、情绪和市场都能画出这条线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wave line that goes up and down and never stays flat.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条上下起伏、始终不平的波浪线。

branches.en: MARKETS AND NUMBERS: prices, rates, sales and currencies are plotted as lines that swing.
branches.cn: 市场与数字：价格、比率、销量和货币被画成摆动的线。

branches.en: MEASURED LEVELS: water, temperature, quality and attendance all move within a range.
branches.cn: 可测水平：水位、温度、质量和出勤率都在一定范围内变动。

branches.en: INNER LIFE: opinions and moods rise and fall without any number attached.
branches.cn: 内心：意见与情绪的起落，并不附着于任何数字。

branches.en: LITERAL WAVE: the original physical movement of a water surface.
branches.cn: 字面波浪：水面原本的物理运动。

branches.en: BETWEEN TWO POLES: the crest and trough of one wave become hope and fear, or one policy and another.
branches.cn: 两极之间：一个波浪的峰与谷变成希望与恐惧，或两种政策。

intro.en: Fluctuate is a Latin verb in -ate built on fluctus. English adds -ion, -ing, -ant, -al and -ly, but the root does the work.
intro.cn: fluctuate 是建立在 fluctus 上的拉丁 -ate 动词。英语加 -ion、-ing、-ant、-al、-ly，但主要靠词根表义。

latinIntro.en: The fluere family is large: fluctus 'wave', fluere 'flow', fluvius 'river', fluentum 'stream'. English has fluent, fluid, flux, influence and superfluous from the same source.
latinIntro.cn: fluere 词族庞大：fluctus“波浪”、fluere“流动”、fluvius“河流”、fluentum“水流”。英语的 fluent、fluid、flux、influence、superfluous 同出一源。

items.meaning: to move in waves; to rise and fall
items.meaningCN: 波动；起伏（fluctus“波浪”+ -ate 动词后缀）

items.meaning: a rise and fall; an irregular change
items.meaningCN: 波动；起伏（-ion 构成动作名词）
items.example: Small fluctuations in temperature are normal.
items.exampleCN: 温度的小幅波动是正常的。

items.meaningCN: 波动的；起伏不定的（-ing 构成形容词）
items.example: A fluctuating supply makes planning hard.
items.exampleCN: 供给波动让规划变得困难。

items.meaningCN: 波动的；起伏的（-ant 构成形容词，医学中也指可移动的）
items.example: The fluctuant mass shifted under pressure.
items.exampleCN: 那个可移动的肿块在按压下移位。

items.meaning: caused by or relating to fluctuation
items.meaningCN: 波动引起的；涨落性的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: Fluctuational noise is hard to filter.

items.meaningCN: 波动地；起伏不定地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The signal fluctuatedly dropped and rose.
items.exampleCN: 信号起伏不定地下降又上升。

items.example: She is fluent in three languages.
items.exampleCN: 她能流利地说三种语言。

items.meaning: a substance that flows; able to change

items.meaningCN: 不断变化；流动；通量（拉丁 fluxus“流动”）
items.example: The system is in a state of flux.
items.exampleCN: 这个系统处于不断变化之中。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 流动；流泻；奔流（fluctuate 的最终词根）
波浪；巨浪；涌动（英语 fluctuate 的直接来源）
起伏；像波浪般运动（英语 fluctuate 的直接拉丁动词）
河流；溪流（同根词，英语 fluvial 的来源）

definition_zh: 波动；涨落；起伏
definition_en: irregular rising and falling in level, amount or condition
core_image: 一条上下起伏的曲线，像水面被风推起的波纹
scene: 这里指「波动」。 Currency fluctuation made the importer's costs change from month to month.
sceneCN: 这里 fluctuation 是「波动」（第 1 个义项：数值上下不规则变化）；句意：汇率波动让进口商的成本逐月变化。图中可辨识物件：汇率曲线、天平、货柜、日历。

senses.title: Prices moving up and down
senses.titleCN: 价格波动：今天高明天低
senses.definition: irregular changes in the price or value of something over time
senses.definitionCN: 某物价格或价值随时间的不规则变化
senses.example: Price fluctuation in the grain market makes planning difficult for farmers.
senses.exampleCN: 粮食市场的价格波动让农民难以规划。
senses.why: fluctus means 'wave'. Prices are pictured as a surface that rises and falls, not as a line that simply goes up.
senses.whyCN: fluctus 意为“波浪”。价格被想象成上下起伏的水面，而不是一条只往上的线。

senses.title: Physical rise and fall
senses.titleCN: 涨落：水位与波动的物理过程
senses.definition: the rising and falling of a physical quantity such as water level or pressure
senses.definitionCN: 水位、压力等物理量的上升与下降
senses.example: The fluctuation of the tide controls when the harbor can be entered.
senses.exampleCN: 潮位的涨落决定何时能进港。
senses.why: This is the literal wave sense. The noun was first used for water and air before it was used for money.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面的波浪义。这个名词先用于水与空气，之后才用于金钱。

senses.title: Statistical variation
senses.titleCN: 统计涨落：平均值附近的抖动
senses.definition: random variation around an average value in measurements or counts
senses.definitionCN: 测量或计数中围绕平均值的随机变化
senses.example: The detector's fluctuation is small enough to be averaged out.
senses.exampleCN: 探测器的涨落小到可以被平均掉。
senses.why: Statistics formalizes the wave: variation is expected, and the word names the up-and-down motion around a mean.
senses.whyCN: 统计学把波浪形式化：变化是预期之中的，这个词命名围绕均值的上下运动。

senses.title: Moods going up and down
senses.titleCN: 情绪起伏：心情像水面一样晃
senses.definition: changes in mood or emotion that go up and down without a fixed pattern
senses.definitionCN: 情绪或心情无固定规律地上下变化
senses.example: Her mood fluctuation worried the people who worked with her.
senses.exampleCN: 她的情绪起伏让共事的人担忧。
senses.why: The metaphor moves inward: feelings are treated as a liquid level that rises and falls, out of the person's control.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻转向内部：情绪被当作会涨落的水位，不受本人控制。

senses.title: Numbers in a population
senses.titleCN: 数量起伏：人多人少来回变
senses.definition: changes in the size of a population, group or quantity over time
senses.definitionCN: 人口、群体或数量随时间的变化
senses.example: The fluctuation of the bird population follows the rainfall cycle.
senses.exampleCN: 鸟类数量的起伏跟随降雨周期。
senses.why: Ecology counts individuals instead of dollars. The shape of the change is the same: not a trend but a repeated rise and fall.
senses.whyCN: 生态学数的是个体而非美元。变化形状相同：不是趋势，而是反复的升降。

senses.title: Quantum fluctuation
senses.titleCN: 量子涨落：真空里短暂的起伏
senses.definition: in physics, a temporary random change in the energy of a quantum system or field
senses.definitionCN: 物理学中指量子系统或场能量的短暂随机变化
senses.example: Quantum fluctuation explains why empty space is never perfectly empty.
senses.exampleCN: 量子涨落解释了为何真空从不是完美的空。
senses.why: The word reaches its most technical point here: a value that briefly departs from its expected level and returns, like a ripple in nothing.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在这里达到最技术化的程度：数值短暂离开期望水平又回来，像“无”中的一圈涟漪。

senses.title: Business cycles
senses.titleCN: 经济波动：繁荣与萧条交替
senses.definition: the recurring expansion and contraction of economic activity
senses.definitionCN: 经济活动的周期性扩张与收缩
senses.example: The study links employment fluctuation to the investment cycle.
senses.exampleCN: 该研究把就业波动与投资周期联系起来。
senses.why: Large-scale economics uses the plural almost always: fluctuations are many waves, not one. The word pictures an economy breathing in and out.
senses.whyCN: 宏观经济学几乎总用复数：波动是许多道浪，不是一道。这个词把经济画成在吸气与呼气。

senses.title: Any irregular change
senses.titleCN: 起伏不定：没有稳定的时候
senses.definition: any change that repeatedly moves away from and back toward a previous level
senses.definitionCN: 任何反复离开先前水平又返回的变化
senses.example: The fluctuation in his attendance made the coach drop him from the team.
senses.exampleCN: 他出勤的起伏让教练把他踢出了队。
senses.why: The general sense keeps the essential shape: movement that is not a steady climb or fall but an oscillation around a level.
senses.whyCN: 总义保留基本形状：不是稳定的升或降，而是围绕某个水平的摆动。

intro.en: Fluctuation comes from Latin fluctuatio, built on fluctuare 'to move in waves', from fluctus 'a wave', from fluere 'to flow'. The word has described water, then prices, then quantum fields.
intro.cn: fluctuation 来自拉丁 fluctuatio，建立在 fluctuare“波浪式运动”之上，而 fluctus“波浪”又源自 fluere“流动”。这个词先后描述水、价格与量子场。

items.en: fluere meant 'to flow'. Its present participle fluens gives English fluent, and the adjective fluidus gives fluid; the same root underlies influence and affluent with different prefixes.
items.cn: fluere 意为“流动”。其现在分词 fluens 生出英语 fluent，形容词 fluidus 生出 fluid；同一词根也见于 influence、affluent，但前缀不同。

items.en: fluctus meant 'a wave, a billow'. It is a fourth-declension noun from the same verb, naming the result of flowing.
items.cn: fluctus 意为“波浪、涌浪”。它是同一动词派生的第四变格名词，命名“流动”的结果。

items.en: fluctuare 'to wave, to move like a wave' turns the noun into a verb. The motion is not directional; it rises and falls around a level.
items.cn: fluctuare“波动、像波浪一样运动”把名词变成动词。这种运动没有固定方向，而是围绕某个水平上下。

items.en: fluctuatio names the action or state of waving. English borrows this form as fluctuation in the 17th century, first for physical motion.
items.cn: fluctuatio 命名“波动”的动作或状态。英语于 17 世纪以 fluctuation 借入这一形式，最初用于物理运动。

items.en: From the 18th and 19th centuries the word spreads to prices, markets and populations, where the up-and-down shape is statistical rather than physical.
items.cn: 18 至 19 世纪，这个词扩展到价格、市场与人口，其上下形状变为统计性的而非物理性的。

items.en: In the 20th century quantum physics adopts the word for short-lived random variations of a field, the smallest possible waves.
items.cn: 20 世纪量子物理采用该词，指场中短暂随机的变化，即最小的波浪。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the flu- root but splits into flow, wave and adjective forms; the near-meaning group all describe change, with different shapes.
note.cn: 形近组共享 flu- 词根，但分为流动、波浪与形容词形式；近义组都描述变化，但形状不同。

entries.definition: to rise and fall irregularly. It is the action; fluctuation is the resulting movement as a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 不规则地上下波动。它是动作；fluctuation 是作为名词的波动。

entries.definition: speaking or flowing smoothly. It comes from the present participle of fluere 'flow', so it describes smooth flow, not wave motion.
entries.definitionCN: 流利的；流畅的。它来自 fluere“流动”的现在分词，因此描述顺畅流动，而非波浪。

entries.definition: a substance that flows; also smooth or changeable. It names flow, while fluctuation names oscillation.
entries.definitionCN: 流体；流动的；易变的。它命名“流”，而 fluctuation 命名“摆”。

entries.definition: a change or difference in condition or level. It is broader and need not go up and down.
entries.definitionCN: 状态或水平的变化或差异。它更宽泛，不必上下反复。

entries.definition: regular movement back and forth. It is more regular than fluctuation, which is often irregular.
entries.definitionCN: 有规律的往返运动。它比 fluctuation 更规则，后者常不规则。

entries.definition: the quality of being likely to change or fail. It judges the change as a problem, while fluctuation merely describes it.
entries.definitionCN: 易变或易失稳的性质。它把变化判定为问题，而 fluctuation 只作描述。

entries.definition: a noticeable change from one level or opinion to another. It is informal and usually suggests a bigger range.
entries.definitionCN: 从一个水平或立场到另一个的明显变化。它口语化，通常暗示幅度更大。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: fluere 'flow' gives fluctus 'wave': fluctuation is a level flowing up and down.
normal.cn: fluere“流动”生出 fluctus“波浪”：fluctuation 就是水平面上下流动。

normal.en: fluent, fluid and fluctuation share the flu- stem but split into smooth flow, substance and oscillation.
normal.cn: fluent、fluid、fluctuation 共享 flu- 词干，但分别指向顺畅流动、流体与摆动。

normal.en: price fluctuation, market fluctuation and exchange-rate fluctuation are the three everyday collocations.
normal.cn: price fluctuation、market fluctuation、exchange-rate fluctuation 是三个日常搭配。

normal.en: Quantum fluctuation is the smallest wave: a value briefly leaves its level and returns.
normal.cn: 量子涨落是最小的波浪：数值短暂离开原位又回来。

normal.en: Fluctuation is neutral, instability is negative; one describes the motion, the other judges it.
normal.cn: fluctuation 中性，instability 负面；一个描述运动，一个评判运动。

abstract.en: Think of a cork bobbing on water, rising and sinking without travelling anywhere.
abstract.cn: 想象一个软木塞在水上上下浮动，却没有去往任何地方。

abstract.en: Think of a graph line that keeps crossing its own average, again and again.
abstract.cn: 想象一条曲线反复穿过自己的平均值。

abstract.en: Think of a heartbeat monitor: the line is never flat, and that is what life looks like.
abstract.cn: 想象心跳监护仪：线从不平直，而生命就是这个样子。

examples.en: Small fluctuations in temperature can change the result of the experiment.
examples.cn: 温度的微小波动就能改变实验结果。

examples.en: The central bank tries to limit fluctuation in the currency.
examples.cn: 央行试图限制货币的波动。

examples.en: Seasonal fluctuation in demand is normal in the tourism industry.
examples.cn: 旅游业的季节性需求波动是正常的。

dict_mnemonic.text: “浮（flu）起来又沉下去”——水面上下浮沉，像价格线来回走 → fluctuation 波动

root: 拉丁 fluere“流动” → fluctus“波浪” → fluctuare“波动” → fluctuatio；核心是“围绕某一水平的上下起伏”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one shape: a level rises and falls around a mean, never settling and never simply climbing.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享一种形状：某个水平围绕均值上下，既不安定，也不是单纯上升。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a water surface pushed into ripples by wind.
core.cn: 核心意象：被风推起波纹的水面。

branches.en: MARKETS: price and business-cycle fluctuation are the same wave seen in a day and in a decade.
branches.cn: 市场：价格波动与经济周期波动，是同一种波浪在一天与十年两个尺度上的样子。

branches.en: PHYSICAL: tide and pressure fluctuation are the literal water-and-air version of the word.
branches.cn: 物理：潮位与压力涨落，是这个词字面上的水与空气版本。

branches.en: RANDOMNESS: statistical variation and quantum fluctuation are small departures from an expected level.
branches.cn: 随机性：统计涨落与量子涨落，都是对期望水平的微小偏离。

branches.en: LIVING THINGS: mood and population fluctuation move the wave from matter to feeling and to counts of organisms.
branches.cn: 生命：情绪与数量波动，把这道浪从物质移到情感与生物计数。

branches.en: GENERAL SHAPE: any repeated departure and return is the same oscillation, whatever the unit.
branches.cn: 一般形状：任何反复离开又返回的运动都是同一种摆动，不论单位是什么。

intro.en: Fluctuation is fluctuate plus -ion. The flu- stem means 'flow', -ct- marks the wave noun, -ate makes a verb and -ion names the motion.
intro.cn: fluctuation 是 fluctuate 加 -ion。flu- 词干意为“流动”，-ct- 标记波浪名词，-ate 构成动词，-ion 命名运动。

latinIntro.en: The family runs from fluere 'flow' to fluctus 'wave' to fluctuare 'wave' to fluctuatio. English relatives include fluent, fluid, influence and affluent.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词族从 fluere“流动”到 fluctus“波浪”到 fluctuare“波动”再到 fluctuatio。英语同族词包括 fluent、fluid、influence、affluent。

items.meaningCN: 波动；起伏（-ate 动词后缀）
items.exampleCN: 整个夏天价格都在波动。

items.meaning: the motion of rising and falling
items.meaningCN: 波动；涨落（-ion 动作名词）
items.example: The fluctuation was within five percent.
items.exampleCN: 波动幅度在百分之五以内。

items.meaningCN: 波动的（-ing 分词形容词）
items.example: The fluctuating demand strained the supply chain.
items.exampleCN: 波动的需求让供应链吃紧。

items.meaning: wavy, moving up and down, now rare
items.meaningCN: 波动的（-ant 形容词，罕用）
items.example: The fluctuant surface made landing difficult.
items.exampleCN: 起伏的水面让降落很困难。

items.meaning: relating to fluctuation, used in physics
items.meaningCN: 涨落的（-al 关系形容词，物理学用）
items.example: Fluctuational noise sets the limit of the sensor.
items.exampleCN: 涨落噪声决定了传感器的极限。

items.meaningCN: 流利的（fluere 现在分词，同一词根）
items.example: She is fluent in three languages.
items.exampleCN: 她能流利使用三种语言。

items.meaningCN: 流体；易变的（-idus 形容词）
items.example: The fluid in the pipe was replaced.
items.exampleCN: 管道里的流体被更换了。

items.meaning: a flowing-in of power or effect
items.meaningCN: 影响（in-“进入”+ fluere“流动”，同根不同义）
items.example: The climate has a strong influence on crops.
items.exampleCN: 气候对作物有很大影响。

definition_zh: 流利的；流畅的；熟练的
definition_en: able to speak a language smoothly, or moving and expressed with ease
core_image: 一个人说着外语，句子像水一样连续不断地流出来
scene: 她说一口流利的英语。She speaks fluent English.
sceneCN: 这里 fluent 是「流利的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她说一口流利的英语。

senses.title: Smooth speech
senses.definition: able to speak a language easily and well
senses.definitionCN: 能轻松而出色地说一门语言
senses.example: She speaks fluent English.
senses.exampleCN: 她说一口流利的英语。
senses.why: This is the most common modern sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是现代最常见的义项。

senses.title: Smooth expression
senses.definition: expressed in a smooth, natural way
senses.definitionCN: 以流畅自然的方式表达的
senses.example: His writing is clear and fluent.
senses.exampleCN: 他的文章清晰流畅。
senses.why: The idea of smooth flow extends to writing.
senses.whyCN: 流畅的概念延伸到写作。

senses.title: Skilled movement
senses.definition: moving with ease and skill
senses.definitionCN: 轻松而熟练地移动
senses.example: The dancer made fluent movements.
senses.exampleCN: 舞者的动作流畅熟练。
senses.why: Smooth language and smooth motion share one image.
senses.whyCN: 流畅的语言与流畅的动作共享一个意象。

intro.en: Fluent comes from Latin fluere, to flow.
intro.cn: fluent 来自拉丁语 fluere，意为流动。

items.en: Fluere meant to flow like water.
items.cn: fluere 意为像水一样流动。

items.en: Fluens described something flowing freely.
items.cn: fluens 形容自由流动的东西。

items.en: Fluent described smooth, flowing speech.
items.cn: fluent 形容流畅的言语。

items.en: Fluent extended to writing and movement.
items.cn: fluent 扩展到写作与动作。

items.en: Fluency became a goal for language learners.
items.cn: fluency 成为语言学习者的目标。

note.en: Fluent is compared with similar-looking words and with words for ease and flow.
note.cn: 把 fluent 与形近词以及表示轻松和流动的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Fluent speech flows like water: no bumps, no stops.
normalIntro.cn: fluent 的语言像水一样流：不磕绊、不停顿。

normal.en: She is fluent in English.
He gave a fluent speech.
normal.cn: 他做了一次流畅的演讲。

normal.en: Her fluent French impressed us.
normal.cn: 她流利的法语让我们印象深刻。

normal.en: Practice makes you more fluent.
The dancer moved in a fluent way.

abstract.en: Fluency hides years of practice.
abstract.cn: 流利掩盖了多年的练习。

abstract.en: Water and words both find the easy path.
abstract.cn: 水与话语都会找到顺畅的路径。

abstract.en: A fluent line never shows where it stopped.
abstract.cn: 流畅的线条从不停下来给人看。

examples.en: She speaks fluent English.
examples.cn: 她说一口流利的英语。

examples.en: His writing is clear and fluent.
examples.cn: 他的文章清晰流畅。

examples.en: The dancer made fluent movements.
examples.cn: 舞者的动作流畅熟练。

dict_mnemonic.text: fluent 的词根 flu 就是「流」，说话像流水一样不断，就是流利。

root: 源自拉丁语 fluere（流动），核心义「像水一样顺畅地流出」。

sensesIntro.en: Fluent means smooth in speech, smooth in expression, or skilled in movement.
sensesIntro.cn: fluent 意为语言流利的、表达流畅的或动作熟练的。

core.en: Words or movement that flow without effort.
core.cn: 毫不费力地流动的话语或动作。

branches.en: Speech that runs like water.
Writing with no rough joins.
Motion that shows no strain.
Speech and writing share the same smoothness.
branches.cn: 口语与写作共享同一种流畅。

branches.en: Skill makes both words and bodies flow.
branches.cn: 技巧让话语与身体都流动起来。

intro.en: Fluent forms a family of flow and smoothness words.
intro.cn: fluent 形成一个表示流动与顺畅的词族。

latinIntro.en: Fluent contains Latin fluere, to flow, a root shared with fluid and flush.
latinIntro.cn: fluent 含有拉丁语 fluere（流动），与 fluid、flush 共享词根。

items.exampleCN: 他的流利程度随练习提高。

items.example: The influent stream feeds the lake.
They live in an affluent area.

items.exampleCN: 两条汇流的河在此相遇。

items.example: The refluent tide pulled the boat.
items.exampleCN: 倒流的潮水拉动了小船。

definition_zh: 飞；飞翔；乘飞机；驾驶飞机；飞逝
definition_en: to move through the air, travel by plane, pilot an aircraft, wave in the wind, or pass quickly
core_image: 一只鸟张开翅膀，越过湖面飞向远处的树林
scene: 鸟飞过湖面。A bird flew over the lake.
sceneCN: 这里 fly 是「飞」（第 1 个义项）；句意：鸟飞过湖面。

senses.title: Move through air
senses.definition: to move through the air with wings or power
senses.definitionCN: 靠翅膀或动力在空中移动
senses.example: A bird flew over the lake.
senses.exampleCN: 鸟飞过湖面。
senses.why: This is the basic physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的物理义项。

senses.title: Travel by plane
senses.definition: to travel in an aircraft
senses.definitionCN: 乘坐飞机旅行
senses.example: We will fly to Beijing tomorrow.
senses.exampleCN: 我们明天乘飞机去北京。
senses.why: People fly as passengers too.
senses.whyCN: 人也能作为乘客飞行。

senses.title: Pilot
senses.definition: to control an aircraft in flight
senses.definitionCN: 操控飞行中的飞机
senses.example: She flies a small plane.
senses.exampleCN: 她驾驶一架小飞机。
senses.why: The verb can name the pilot's action.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词也可指飞行员的操作。

senses.title: Wave in air
senses.definition: to move freely in the wind
senses.definitionCN: 在风中自由飘动
senses.example: Flags fly above the square.
senses.exampleCN: 旗帜在广场上空飘扬。
senses.why: Cloth moves through air like a wing.
senses.whyCN: 布像翅膀一样在空中移动。

senses.title: Pass quickly
senses.definition: to pass very quickly
senses.definitionCN: 非常快地过去
senses.example: The summer flew by.
senses.exampleCN: 夏天飞快地过去了。
senses.why: Time is imagined as flying.
senses.whyCN: 时间被想象成在飞。

intro.en: Fly comes from an Old English word for moving through the air.
intro.cn: fly 来自古英语中表示在空中移动的词。

items.en: Fleogan meant to fly with wings.
items.cn: fleogan 意为用翅膀飞行。

items.en: Fleuganan carried the same airy sense.
items.cn: fleuganan 带有同样的空中含义。

items.en: Fly extended to travel by aircraft.
items.cn: fly 扩展到乘飞机旅行。

items.en: Fly described flags and hair moving in wind.
items.cn: fly 形容旗帜和头发在风中飘动。

items.en: Time flies became a common saying.
items.cn: time flies 成为常用俗语。

note.en: Fly is compared with similar-looking words and with words for air travel.
note.cn: 把 fly 与形近词以及表示空中飞行的词作比较。

entries.definition: to fly high in the air
to go from one place to another

normalIntro.en: Fly is a bird, a passenger, a pilot, a flag, and time itself moving through air.
normalIntro.cn: fly 可以是鸟、乘客、飞行员、旗帜，也可以是穿过空气的时间。

normal.en: Birds fly south in winter.
We fly to Shanghai on Monday.
normal.cn: 我们周一乘飞机去上海。

normal.en: He flies a helicopter.
The flag flies in the wind.
Time flies when you are busy.

abstract.en: A plane is a metal bird with a schedule.
abstract.cn: 飞机是一只有时刻表的金属鸟。

abstract.en: Flags fly because they are tied down.
abstract.cn: 旗帜能飘扬是因为它被系住了。

abstract.en: Time flies only when we look back.
abstract.cn: 只有回头看时，时间才显得飞快。

examples.en: A bird flew over the lake.
examples.cn: 鸟飞过湖面。

examples.en: We will fly to Beijing tomorrow.
examples.cn: 我们明天乘飞机去北京。

examples.en: The summer flew by.
examples.cn: 夏天飞快地过去了。

dict_mnemonic.text: fly 的核心是「离地而行」：鸟飞、人坐飞机飞、旗子被风带着飞、时间也飞。

root: 源自古英语 fleogan（用翅膀飞行），核心义「在空中移动」。

sensesIntro.en: Fly means to move through air, travel by plane, pilot a plane, wave in wind, or pass quickly.
sensesIntro.cn: fly 意为飞、乘飞机、驾驶飞机、飘动或飞逝。

core.en: Leaving the ground and moving through air.
core.cn: 离开地面并在空中移动。

branches.en: A bird beats its wings and rises.
A passenger boards a plane.
A pilot controls the aircraft.
Cloth waves in the wind.
Time seems to pass on wings.

intro.en: Fly forms a family of flight and travel words.
intro.cn: fly 形成一个表示飞行与旅行的词族。

latinIntro.en: Fly has no Latin ancestor; Latin volare, to fly, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: fly 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 volare（飞）只是语义对应词。

items.example: The eagle flies above the valley.
She flies every week for work.
They flew to Tokyo last night.
He has flown this route for years.
Flying fish leap from the water.

items.meaning: a pilot or a printed sheet

definition_zh: 焦点；聚焦；集中；重点
definition_en: the point where light or attention meets, or to direct attention or a lens there
core_image: 放大镜把阳光聚成一点，纸面冒起一缕烟
scene: 请把注意力集中在题目上。Please focus on the question.
sceneCN: 这里 focus 是「集中」（第 2 个义项）；句意：请把注意力集中在题目上。

senses.title: Point of light
senses.definition: the point where rays of light meet
senses.definitionCN: 光线汇聚的那一点
senses.example: Adjust the lens until the image is in focus.
senses.exampleCN: 调节镜头直到图像清晰对焦。
senses.why: This is the original optical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最初的光学义项。

senses.title: To concentrate
senses.definition: to direct attention toward something
senses.definitionCN: 把注意力引向某事物
senses.example: Please focus on the question.
senses.exampleCN: 请把注意力集中在题目上。
senses.why: Attention is treated like a beam of light.
senses.whyCN: 注意力被当作一束光。

senses.title: To adjust a lens
senses.definition: to make an image clear by moving a lens
senses.definitionCN: 移动镜头使图像清晰
senses.example: She focused the camera on the bird.
senses.exampleCN: 她把相机对准鸟儿对焦。
senses.why: The verb keeps the optical action.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留了光学的动作。

senses.title: Main point
senses.definition: the central subject of attention
senses.definitionCN: 注意力的中心主题
senses.example: Cost is the main focus of the report.
senses.exampleCN: 成本是这份报告的重点。
senses.why: The meeting point of rays becomes a topic.
senses.whyCN: 光线的汇聚点引申为话题。

intro.en: Focus is Latin for hearth, the fireplace at the centre of a home.
intro.cn: focus 在拉丁语中意为壁炉，即家宅中央的火塘。

items.en: Focus meant a hearth or fireplace.
items.cn: focus 意为壁炉或火塘。

items.en: Opticians used focus for the point of rays.
items.cn: 光学家用 focus 表示光线的汇聚点。

items.en: Focus entered English as an optical term.
items.cn: focus 作为光学术语进入英语。

items.en: Focus extended to attention and importance.
items.cn: focus 扩展到注意力与重要性。

items.en: Focus became a common verb meaning concentrate.
items.cn: focus 成为表示集中的常用动词。

note.en: Focus is compared with similar-looking words and with words for attention and centres.
note.cn: 把 focus 与形近词以及表示注意力和中心的词作比较。

entries.definition: trickery, used in the phrase hocus-pocus
the act of watching or listening carefully

normalIntro.en: Focus is a meeting point: light, attention, or the main topic all gather there.
normalIntro.cn: focus 是一个汇聚点：光、注意力或主要话题都在那里聚集。

normal.en: Focus on your homework.
The camera is in focus.
The main focus is safety.
He lost focus during the lecture.
Focus the light on the paper.

abstract.en: Attention is a beam you can point.
abstract.cn: 注意力是一束可以指向的光。

abstract.en: A clear focus leaves the rest blurred.
abstract.cn: 清晰的焦点让其余部分变模糊。

abstract.en: A hearth and a lens both gather people and light.
abstract.cn: 火塘聚人，镜头聚光。

examples.en: Please focus on the question.
examples.cn: 请把注意力集中在题目上。

examples.en: She focused the camera on the bird.
examples.cn: 她把相机对准鸟儿对焦。

examples.en: Cost is the main focus of the report.
examples.cn: 成本是这份报告的重点。

dict_mnemonic.text: focus 原指家中火塘，是一家人目光汇聚之处；后来指光线汇聚的焦点，再指注意力的集中点。

root: 源自拉丁语 focus（火塘、壁炉），核心义「汇聚的中心点」。

sensesIntro.en: Focus means an optical point, to concentrate, to adjust a lens, or the main point.
sensesIntro.cn: focus 意为焦点、集中、对焦或重点。

core.en: A point where rays or attention come together.
core.cn: 光线或注意力汇聚的一点。

branches.en: Light rays meet at one point.
The mind gathers on one task.
branches.cn: 心思聚集在一项任务上。

branches.en: The lens is moved until clear.
A report centres on one subject.
Light and attention follow the same geometry.
branches.cn: 光与注意力遵循同样的几何。

intro.en: Focus forms a family of attention and lens words.
intro.cn: focus 形成一个表示注意力与镜头的词族。

latinIntro.en: Focus is a Latin word for hearth; it has no productive Latin affixes.
latinIntro.cn: focus 是拉丁语中表示火塘的词；它在拉丁语中没有能产后缀。

items.exampleCN: 她给出了重点明确的回答。

items.example: Let us refocus on the plan.

items.meaning: a camera system that focuses itself
items.exampleCN: 这部手机自动对焦很快。

definition_zh: 折叠；合拢；交叠；倒闭；羊圈
definition_en: to bend something over on itself, to close, to fail as a business, or a pen for sheep
core_image: 双手把一张信纸对折，压出整齐的折痕
scene: 她把信折好放进信封。She folded the letter and put it in the envelope.
sceneCN: 这里 fold 是「折叠」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她把信折好放进信封。

senses.title: Bend over
senses.definition: to bend something so that one part lies on another
senses.definitionCN: 弯曲某物使一部分叠在另一部分上
senses.example: She folded the letter and put it in the envelope.
senses.exampleCN: 她把信折好放进信封。
senses.why: This is the basic physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的物理义项。

senses.title: Cross arms
senses.definition: to cross one's arms or hands
senses.definitionCN: 交叉双臂或双手
senses.example: He folded his arms and waited.
senses.exampleCN: 他交叉双臂等着。
senses.why: Body parts fold like paper.
senses.whyCN: 身体部位像纸一样折叠。

senses.title: Close down
senses.definition: to close a business after failure
senses.definitionCN: 经营失败后关闭企业
senses.example: The shop folded after a year.
senses.exampleCN: 那家店一年后就倒闭了。
senses.why: A failing business closes like a folded chair.
senses.whyCN: 失败的企业像折起的椅子一样合上。

senses.title: Sheep pen
senses.definition: an enclosed area where sheep are kept
senses.definitionCN: 圈养羊的围栏区域
senses.example: The farmer led the sheep into the fold.
senses.exampleCN: 农夫把羊领进羊圈。
senses.why: This old noun sense has its own origin.
senses.whyCN: 这个古老的名词义项另有来源。

intro.en: The verb fold comes from Old English fealdan; the sheep pen fold comes from a different Old English word.
intro.cn: 动词 fold 来自古英语 fealdan；羊圈义的 fold 来自另一个古英语词。

items.en: Fealdan meant to bend or wrap.
items.cn: fealdan 意为弯曲或包裹。

items.en: Fald meant a pen for sheep.
items.cn: fald 意为圈羊的围栏。

items.en: Folden kept the sense of bending cloth and paper.
items.cn: folden 保留了折布折纸的含义。

items.en: Fold described closing a business.
items.cn: fold 开始形容企业关闭。

items.en: Fold became common in computing and design.
items.cn: fold 在计算机与设计领域变得常见。

note.en: Fold is compared with similar-looking words and with words for bending and closing.
note.cn: 把 fold 与形近词以及表示弯曲和关闭的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: To fold is to make one surface meet another and leave a line behind.
normalIntro.cn: fold 就是让两个面相遇，并留下一条折痕。

normal.en: Fold the paper in half.
He folded his arms.
Fold up the chair after use.
The business folded last year.
The sheep slept in the fold.

abstract.en: A folded map hides more than it shows.
abstract.cn: 折起的地图藏起的比显示的多。

abstract.en: Some businesses fold like paper chairs.
abstract.cn: 有些企业像纸椅一样折倒。

abstract.en: A crease remembers every fold.
abstract.cn: 折痕记得每一次折叠。

examples.en: She folded the letter and put it in the envelope.
examples.cn: 她把信折好放进信封。

examples.en: He folded his arms and waited.
examples.cn: 他交叉双臂等着。

examples.en: The shop folded after a year.
examples.cn: 那家店一年后就倒闭了。

dict_mnemonic.text: fold 的核心是「一面向另一面靠拢」：折纸、抱臂、关店，都是合起来。

root: 动词源自古英语 fealdan（弯曲、包裹）；羊圈义源自古英语 fald。

sensesIntro.en: Fold means to bend over, cross the arms, close a business, or a sheep pen.
sensesIntro.cn: fold 意为折叠、交叠、倒闭或羊圈。

core.en: One surface laid over another.
core.cn: 一个面叠在另一个面上。

branches.en: Paper bent into two layers.
Arms crossed over the chest.
A business closing its doors.
A pen that holds sheep together.
Paper folds and businesses fold, both closing up.
branches.cn: 纸会折，企业会倒，都是合拢。

intro.en: Fold forms a family of bending and closing words.
intro.cn: fold 形成一个表示弯曲与合拢的词族。

latinIntro.en: Fold has no Latin ancestor; Latin plicare, to fold, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: fold 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 plicare（折叠）只是语义对应词。

items.example: The napkin was folded into a swan.
Put the report in the folder.
The phone has a foldable screen.
items.exampleCN: 这部手机有可折叠屏幕。

items.example: Unfold the map on the table.

definition_zh: 叶子（总称）；叶丛；装饰用枝叶
definition_en: the leaves of a plant or of many plants taken as a mass; cut branches used for decoration
core_image: 一棵树的所有叶片连成一片会摇动的绿色表面，风过时整片一起翻动
scene: 入秋以后叶片由绿转铜再转金，远看整片林子像被重新上了色。Autumn turns the foliage copper and gold.
sceneCN: 这里 foliage 指「一棵或一片植物上全部叶子的总称」（第 1 个义项：把叶子作为整体看待的叶丛）；句意为秋天把叶丛染成铜色与金色。

senses.title: All the leaves of a plant
senses.titleCN: 一株或一片植物的叶子的总称
senses.definition: the leaves of a plant or group of plants considered as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 把一株或一群植物的叶子作为整体看待
senses.example: Autumn turns the foliage copper and gold.
senses.exampleCN: 秋天把叶丛染成铜色与金色。
senses.why: Foliage is a collective noun: it never counts leaves one by one, it sees them as one surface.
senses.whyCN: foliage 是集合名词：它从不一片一片地数叶子，而是把叶子看成一张表面。

senses.title: The leafy canopy as a layer
senses.titleCN: 树冠里由叶子组成的那一层
senses.definition: the layer of leaves that fills a crown and shades what is below
senses.definitionCN: 树冠中填满枝叶、遮住下方的那一层
senses.example: Sparrows hid in the dense foliage of the hedge.
senses.exampleCN: 麻雀藏在树篱茂密的叶丛里。
senses.why: Once the mass is seen from below or above, it becomes a layer with depth and shade, not just a list of parts.
senses.whyCN: 从下方或上方看这团叶子时，它就成了有厚度、有阴影的一层，而不只是一堆部件。

senses.title: Leaves valued for their colour
senses.titleCN: 因颜色而被观赏的叶子
senses.definition: leaves regarded as colour, especially in autumn or in ornamental planting
senses.definitionCN: 被当作色彩来欣赏的叶子，尤指秋叶或观赏栽植
senses.example: Tourists come for the autumn foliage.
senses.exampleCN: 游客为秋叶而来。
senses.why: When colour is the point, the word moves from botany to scenery, and the leaf becomes a patch of paint.
senses.whyCN: 当重点是颜色，这个词就从植物学移向风景，叶子也成了一块颜料。

senses.title: Cut branches for decoration
senses.definition: stems and leaves cut for floristry or display
senses.definitionCN: 为花艺或陈列剪下的枝与叶
senses.example: The florist ordered cut foliage for the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 花艺师为大堂订了切叶。
senses.why: A trade term treats the mass as material: it is harvested, graded and sold like any other stock.
senses.whyCN: 行业术语把这团叶当材料：像别的货品一样采收、分级、出售。

senses.title: Leafy material eaten by animals
senses.definition: branches and leaves used as fodder
senses.definitionCN: 用作饲料的枝叶
senses.example: Goats browse the lower foliage of the trees.
senses.exampleCN: 山羊啃食树下部枝叶。
senses.why: Husbandry turns the same mass into feed, measured by what a animal can reach.
senses.whyCN: 畜牧把它变成饲料，按动物能够到的高度来衡量。

senses.title: Leaf ornament in art
senses.definition: leaf forms used as ornament in architecture or design
senses.definitionCN: 建筑与设计中被用作装饰的叶形
senses.example: The capital is carved with acanthus foliage.
senses.exampleCN: 柱头刻着茛苕叶饰。
senses.why: Ornament keeps only the outline of leaves, so the word comes to mean a pattern rather than a plant.
senses.whyCN: 装饰只保留叶子的轮廓，词义于是变成图案而非植物。

senses.title: A plant grown for its leaves
senses.titleCN: 以观叶为目的栽种的植物
senses.definition: a plant cultivated mainly for its leaves rather than flowers
senses.definitionCN: 主要因叶而非花而栽种的植物
senses.example: Foliage plants fill the shaded border.
senses.exampleCN: 观叶植物填满了背阴花坛。
senses.why: Horticulture splits plants by the organ that sells, and the leaf group takes the mass noun as a label.
senses.whyCN: 园艺按出售的器官给植物分类，观叶这一类就用这个集合名词作标签。

senses.title: Cover and concealment
senses.titleCN: 被枝叶遮住而形成的掩蔽
senses.definition: the concealment that a mass of leaves provides
senses.definitionCN: 成片叶子提供的遮蔽
senses.example: The nest was lost in foliage.
senses.exampleCN: 巢藏在叶丛深处看不见。
senses.why: A mass thick enough to hide a nest becomes a place, so the word shifts from material to cover.
senses.whyCN: 厚到能藏住鸟巢的一团叶就成了一个地方，词义从材料转为掩蔽。

intro.en: Foliage comes from Old French feuillage, from feuille 'leaf', from Latin folium 'leaf'. The Latin noun is linked to Greek phyllon, but the deeper origin is unsettled.
intro.cn: foliage 来自古法语 feuillage，源于 feuille「叶」，再往前是拉丁 folium「叶」。这个拉丁名词与希腊 phyllon 有联系，但更深来源未定。

items.en: Folium meant 'leaf'. Its relation to Greek phyllon 'leaf' is generally believed, yet no single older root has been demonstrated.
items.cn: folium 意为「叶」。它与希腊 phyllon「叶」的联系一般认为成立，但更古老的单一词根尚未得到证明。

items.en: The plural folia 'leaves' was felt as a collective, which prepared the way for a mass noun.
items.cn: 复数 folia「叶子」有集合意味，为后来的集合名词铺了路。

items.en: Old French feuille 'leaf' kept the Latin sense; its collective derivative feuillage named the mass of leaves.
items.cn: 古法语 feuille「叶」保留了拉丁义；它的集合派生词 feuillage 指成片的叶。

items.en: English borrowed foliage in the sixteenth century for leaves in general, and later for cut branches in floristry.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪借入 foliage，泛指叶子，后来又指花艺中的切叶。

items.en: Architectural handbooks extended it to carved leaf patterns, where only the outline survives.
items.cn: 建筑手册把它扩展到雕刻的叶形图案，那里只剩轮廓。

items.en: Source uncertain (root only): the link between folium and phyllon is a general belief rather than a proven derivation, and the first English date is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅词根）：folium 与 phyllon 的联系只是一般看法，并非已证实的派生；英语首见年代为约数。

note.en: Group one separates relatives built on Latin folium from one false friend; group two holds words for leaves and leaf masses.
note.cn: 第一组区分由拉丁 folium 构成的同族词与一个假朋友；第二组指叶子与叶丛的说法。

entries.definition: From folium: a leaf of paper or a book format; the plant sense was lost when it named pages.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 folium：指一张纸或书的开本；转指纸页后植物义消失。

entries.definition: Portare 'to carry' plus folium: a case for loose sheets, now also a set of investments.
entries.definitionCN: portare「携带」加 folium：装散页的夹子，今也指一组投资。

entries.definition: Relating to leaves, as foliar feeding; it describes leaves rather than naming a mass.
entries.definitionCN: 与叶有关的，如叶面施肥；它描述叶，不命名叶丛。

entries.definition: From Latin filum 'thread', which gave the idea of a line of documents; nothing to do with leaves.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 filum「线」，引申为一列文件，与叶子无关。

entries.definition: The plain plural that counts individual leaves; foliage never counts.
entries.definitionCN: 普通复数，一片一片地数；foliage 从不计数。

entries.definition: An English formation on leaf plus -age, close in sense but far rarer than foliage.
entries.definitionCN: 由 leaf 加 -age 的英语构词，意义接近，但远比 foliage 少见。

entries.definition: The whole upper layer of a tree or forest, branches included; foliage is the leaf part of it.
entries.definitionCN: 指树或林的上层，含枝条；foliage 是其中的叶部。

entries.definition: Green plants as a pleasant sight; foliage is the leaf mass itself.
entries.definitionCN: 作为悦目景色的绿色植物；foliage 是叶丛本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin root and the real horticultural terms.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用真实拉丁词根与真实园艺术语。

normal.en: Latin folium 'leaf' + -age (collective): a mass of leaves.
normal.cn: 拉丁 folium「叶」+ -age（集合）：成片的叶子。

normal.en: The family: foliar, foliate, defoliate, foliation.
Fixed phrases: dense foliage, autumn foliage, foliage plant, cut foliage.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：茂密叶丛、秋叶、观叶植物、切叶。

normal.en: The same root gives folio and portfolio, both about sheets of paper.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 folio 与 portfolio，都与纸页有关。

normal.en: Florists sell cut foliage as material, the same way nurseries sell foliage plants.
normal.cn: 花艺师把切叶当材料卖，苗圃则卖观叶植物。

abstract.en: Picture one green surface spread over a whole wood, with no single leaf visible.
abstract.cn: 想象一整片森林上铺着一张绿表面，看不到单独一片叶。

abstract.en: Picture autumn as a painter repainting that surface from green to copper.
abstract.cn: 想象秋天是一位画家，把那层表面从绿改涂成铜色。

abstract.en: Picture a page and a leaf sharing one word because both are thin and flat.
abstract.cn: 想象一页纸与一片叶共用一个词，因为两者都薄而平。

examples.en: The hedge keeps its foliage through the coldest months.
examples.cn: 这道树篱在最冷的几个月里仍保留叶丛。

examples.en: Cut foliage is sold by weight at the flower market.
examples.cn: 切叶在花市按重量出售。

examples.en: Acid rain damaged the foliage of the upland forest.
examples.cn: 酸雨损害了高地森林的叶丛。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「佛利（foli）叶 + 集合（age）」——一大团叶子 → 叶丛；叶子总称

root: 古法语 feuillage 来自 feuille「叶」，再往前是拉丁 folium「叶」；folium 与希腊 phyllon 的联系一般认为成立，更深词根未定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses treat leaves as one mass, then as shade, colour, cut material, fodder, ornament, a plant class and finally a hiding place.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都先把叶子当成一团，再依次当作阴影、颜色、切材、饲料、纹样、植物类别，最后当作藏身之处。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one continuous green surface made of countless leaves.
core.cn: 核心意象：由无数叶片连成的一整张绿色表面。

branches.en: MASS INTO LAYER: a crowd of leaves becomes a canopy with depth.
branches.cn: 成团成层：一堆叶子变成有厚度的一层。

branches.en: COLOUR: the same mass is valued as paint on a landscape.
branches.cn: 颜色：同一团叶被当作风景上的颜料。

branches.en: MATERIAL: cut for the vase or browsed by animals, leaves become stock or feed.
branches.cn: 材料：剪进花瓶或被牲畜啃食，叶子成了货品或饲料。

branches.en: PATTERN AND CLASS: art keeps the outline, horticulture keeps the label.
branches.cn: 纹样与类别：艺术保留轮廓，园艺保留标签。

branches.en: COVER: thick enough to hide a nest, the mass becomes a place.
branches.cn: 掩蔽：厚到能藏巢，这团叶就成了一个地方。

intro.en: Foliage is Latin folium plus a French collective suffix; the root also builds the vocabulary of pages and of defoliation.
intro.cn: foliage 是拉丁 folium 加法语集合后缀；这个词根还构成纸页与落叶方面的词汇。

latinIntro.en: Latin folium 'leaf' gives folia, foliaris and foliatus; -age marks a collective mass in French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 folium「叶」给出 folia、foliaris 与 foliatus；-age 在法语中表示集合。

items.example: The root names the flat green organ.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指扁平的绿色器官。

items.example: The plural was felt as a mass.
items.exampleCN: 这个复数带有集合意味。

items.example: It turns a single leaf into a mass.
A foliated capital shows carved leaves.
items.exampleCN: 有叶饰的柱头刻着叶子。
